text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Tax Minister Carsten Koch is investigating the possibilities of taking legal action against company directors who knowingly sell their firms to asset-strippers.

--- The fall of Conservative leader Hans Engell does not overall weaken the right-wing Conservative-Liberal alliance, a poll conducted over the weekend shows. While Conservative support weakend by close to one percentage point, Liberal backing picked up by about the same amount.
--- Most Danes are tired of tv commercials a new survey shows with 64 percent of viewers questioned finding them irritating and boring and only 23 percent finding them interesting and entertaining.

--- The market for private health insurance and private pension savings is seen growing strongly over the coming years. Health insurance company Sygeforsikringen Danmark, which has the monopoly of health insurance in Denmark, increased premium earnings from 887.2 million in 1992 to 1.3 billion in 1996.
